newsitem.title: USA: US House debate likely Tuesday on CRP extension.
newsitem.headline: US House debate likely Tuesday on CRP extension.

text.p: The U.S. House was expected to debate on Tuesday a bill allowing farmers to unilaterally extend their Conservation Reserve Program contracts by one year, an Agriculture Committee spokesman said Monday.

The bill was listed on the House's suspension calendar, the repository for noncontroversial bills. Debate on those bills is limited to 40 minutes and no amendments are allowed but a two-thirds vote is required for passage.

Under the bill sponsored by Agriculture chairman Bob Smith, Oregon Republican, farmers with fall-planted crops would get a one-year extension to CRP contracts that expire this year if they notified the Agriculture Department that they wanted an extension.
Aides say the bill would affect a few million acres.
